newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI FOREX TRADING HOURS EXTENDED BY ERM.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI FOREX TRADING HOURS EXTENDED BY ERM.

text.p: Interbank forex traders on Monday agreed to trade until 1715/1415 GMT instead of closing the market at 1600/1300 GMT, forex market sources said.
The market will now open between 0900/0600 GMT and 1715/1415 GMT, they said.
The decision followed a Bank of Finland announcement that its responsibility according to the ERM agreement is to keep the markka within its bands between 1000/0700 GMT and 1800/1500 GMT.
"We have agreed to trade until five-fifteen now ... as a result of ERM," a chief dealer said.
However, a central bank intervention officer said the bank had not excluded action at any time in any market.
"We have just announced what our responsibilities are," said Olli-Pekka Lehmussaari at the central bank.
"We have not excluded action at any time ... or anywhere," he said.

Bond market traders said market makers were considering extending trading hours on the bond and money markets too but that no decision had yet been made. The next primary dealer meeting would be held in November.
"I think this is something we will talk about, I personally think it will be inevitable," Merita chief dealer Jussi Silvennoinen said.
"I expect that the (bond) market will have to stay open until something like five or a quarter past," he said.
One problem with the current 1600/1300 GMT close is that it comes just before the release of many U.S. indicators, increasing late volatility, dealers said.
